title: Hackweek 30m Bootcamp: developer-first value props, quickstart angles, pricing language (draft)
content:
Context and goal:

This is a lightweight, testable messaging & onboarding sketch for a 30-minute "hackweek" bootcamp experience aimed at engineers evaluating Redwood's Hosted API. The objective: get an engineer from zero to a minimally delightful demo (streamed chat or summarization) in 30 minutes, while validating pricing language and developer-focused value props that reduce cognitive friction about cost and performance.

Why this is different from existing onramps:
- Emphasize predictable economics up front (cost estimate for the mini-demo, token budgeting), not just feature lists.
- Offer one-minute wins (hello-world call <60s), then a 20-minute guided lab, then a 9-minute cost/scale explainer + next steps.
- Position Redwood as the infrastructure tradeoff layer: same API surface whether you later choose hosted, dedicated, or private.

High-level flow (30m):
1) 0-2m: Welcome and "What you'll build" one-sentence pitch + expected cost ("~$0.06 for this demo").
2) 2-6m: Create API key, run the hello-world text generation (curl + node snippet).
3) 6-18m: Guided lab: add streaming, add simple function-calling, or call embeddings for a search demo (choose one path).
4) 18-25m: Inspect cost & latency metrics in Console mock (token breakdown), show batching/quantization tips in 3 bullets.
5) 25-30m: Next steps CTAs (start free credits, schedule Dedicated consult, import model via Private trial).

Core developer-first value propositions to test in copy (short variants):
- V1 (speed): "From zero to a streaming demo in 30 minutes — one API, no infra setup."
- V2 (economics): "Know exactly what your prototype costs: per-demo estimates and token previews before you run."
- V3 (portability): "Same code works for hosted, dedicated, and private — build once, deploy anywhere."
- V4 (reliability): "Built-in fallbacks keep your app online if capacity drops — no surprise outages during demos."

Pricing-language experiments (microcopy + rationale):
- Anchor line A: "Starter demo: ~100–500 tokens, ~ $0.03–$0.12 — we show an estimate before you run." (aims to remove sticker shock).
- Anchor line B (trial): "Free credits cover 50 demo runs of the 30m bootcamp" (aims to encourage repeated attempts).
- Anchor line C (scaling signal): "When you scale, Reserved capacity gives a predictable monthly bill and SLA — estimate available in the console."
- Experiment: show an inline calculator during the guided lab vs. only a post-run receipt. Measure conversion and perceived clarity.

Suggested microcopy snippets for UI / email / landing:
- Landing hero: "Build a live LLM feature in 30 minutes — predictable cost, production-ready controls."
- SDK quickstart tooltip: "Estimate: ~ $0.08 for this run (50 tokens + 150-generation tokens)."
- End-of-lab CTA: "Keep the same API. Upgrade to Dedicated for predictable throughput — we'll show the math."

Competitive notes (concise bullets for SDRs/solutions engineers):
- OpenAI: Strong brand and broad features. Weakness: less transparent per-request economics and no unified private/dedicated migration flow in our target messaging. Opportunity: emphasize our cost/portability story.
- Anthropic: Developer-friendly model safety and chat-first UX. Weakness: complexity around private deployments for enterprises. Opportunity: contrast with our private-first control plane and rollout tools.
- Self-host + Inference runtimes (Replicate, Ollama, self-managed): Lower per-token cost potential but higher ops overhead. Opportunity: pitch Redwood as "best of both": managed hosted with an easy migration path to dedicated/private and tooling that reduces ops lift.

Metrics and signals to capture during the experiment (primary + secondary):
- Primary: time-to-first-token (target < 3 minutes), demo completion rate within 30m, % users who view cost estimate before running.
- Secondary: free-credit redemption rate, retention (return within 7 days), ticket or demo request conversion to sales conversation.
- Instrumentation notes: capture token counts for the demo, latency percentiles, and which pricing microcopy variant was shown.

Hypotheses & A/B tests (prioritized):
- H1: Showing an up-front estimated cost increases demo completion by 18% (A: estimate before run, B: no estimate).
- H2: "Build once, deploy anywhere" copy increases requests for Dedicated/Private consults (track clicks on 'Dedicated estimate' CTA).
- H3: Inline cost calculator while editing prompts reduces support questions about billing.

Guided lab variants (fast experiments):
- Path A (Streaming chat): focuses on streaming and latency controls. Steps: hello call -> enable stream -> show Console latency chart -> toggle batch size suggestion.
- Path B (Search + Embeddings): generate embeddings -> simple vector search -> present per-query cost and suggest caching.
- Path C (Tooling + Function calling): call a mock external tool (e.g., weather API) via function call, demonstrate structured output + reduced token usage via function args.

Tiny code snippets to include in the bootcamp (display as plain text in docs / UI):
- Curl quickstart (node SDK alternative provided):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rwd-gpt-3b", "input":"Summarize: Why Redwood for inference?"}'

- Node minimal streaming example (pseudocode):
  const client = new RedwoodClient({apiKey: process.env.RWD_KEY});
  const stream = await client.generateStream({model: 'rwd-chat-3b', messages: [{role:'user', content:'Explain Redwood in one paragraph'}]});
  stream.on('data', chunk => process.stdout.write(chunk.text));

Cost/Console mockups to test (quick visuals we can hand to design):
- In-line estimate badge above run button (green for <$0.10, amber for $0.10-1.00, red for >$1).
- Post-run token breakdown modal (prompt tokens, generated tokens, embedding tokens) with dollar amounts and per-token rate shown.
- "What this means at scale" modal showing a 1M query projection with options: keep Hosted (show cost), switch to Dedicated (show monthly commit), or Private (show engineering cost estimate).

Operational checklist for running the experiment during Hackweek:
- Product: create the 30m guided lab in the quickstarts repo (GH PR linked above).
- Console: add static mockups and a telemetry flag to record microcopy variant.
- Growth/GTM: create the landing + 1-email drip for participants; tag traffic sources.
- SRE/infra: confirm test tokens and a safe throttling policy for bootcamp runs.
- Design: produce the 3 quick mockups (estimate badge, token breakdown modal, scaling modal).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Users misinterpret the estimate and think they will always pay that exact amount. Mitigation: small tooltip: "Approximate — actual cost depends on tokens generated."
- Risk: Friction from requiring API key before hello-world. Mitigation: offer a sandbox key that auto-expire and clearly label it.

Next immediate steps (week 0):
1) Lock copy variants for the landing & tooltips (Maya + Priya).
2) PR for quickstart lab (Noah to author the GH PR).
3) Instrument telemetry flags and metrics dashboard (Liam + Growth).
4) Schedule 1-hour usability run with 8 engineers during Hackweek (measure time-to-first-token).

Open questions (to resolve in next sync):
- What is the default cost estimate thresholds for badge coloring? (design+finance)
- How many free credits do we advertise on the landing vs. in email follow-up? (growth)
- Which demo path most closely correlates to enterprise interest (chat vs. embeddings)? We should instrument and pivot quickly.

Appendix: quick list of microcopy alternatives to test (each <= 10 words):
- "Start in 30 minutes, see per-demo cost before you run."
- "Try hosting now — switch to Dedicated when you need predictability."
- "Estimate your demo cost — transparency by design."
- "Free credits for a limited number of bootcamp runs."

End of draft.

Notes: keep this doc live during Hackweek; after the experiment, convert learnings into a concise playbook for onboarding new developers.
